newsitem.title: FRANCE: GOLF-LYLE RETURNS TO EUROPE OPTIMISTIC.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-LYLE RETURNS TO EUROPE OPTIMISTIC.

text.p: Sandy Lyle, former British Open and US Masters champion, plays his first European Tour event of the season when he tees up in the French Open in Paris on Thursday seeking to end the poor run of form he has had on the American tour.
Lyle, 39, the 1985 British Open winner and 1988 US Masters champion, has not played on the European Tour since the fourth-last event of 1996, finishing 128th in Europe from 10 starts.
The Scot decided to play on the US Tour again this year. He has two more season's exemption there through his past achievements, including this campaign.

His form has been inconsistent in America. He finished 34th in this year's US Masters and had a good start in the Tournament Players Championship at Jacksonville, where he has set up home, but then faded badly.
He is struggling way down the American Order of Merit and hopes his short stay in Europe can fire his year over the Atlantic.
"I have three events in Europe -- this week, the Loch Lomond World Invitational and the British Open -- and it would be nice to get back some form where it all started for me," Lyle said.
"It's not been good in America. I've only earned about $60,000 and I daren't look at the Order of Merit, although it only takes one good weekend, a second or third, and you can get right up there.

"I need a confidence boost. When I lost out to Ian Woosnam in the Korean Masters a few weeks ago my form then gave me a bit of confidence and the work I'm doing with my coach, just keeping it simple, has given me a base to make a comeback. I'm still young enough to win tournaments."
He harbours hopes of a good British Open, admitting he has taken next week's Irish Open off "to get in a few sneaky practice rounds at Royal Troon".

Top attraction at the French National course is four-times European number one Colin Montgomerie, bidding for a record five titles in succession. The Scot can move to within 80,000 pounds ($133,000) of current Order of Merit leader Welshman Woosnam if he takes the 100,000 pounds first prize in his first event back since finishing runner-up to Ernie Els in the US Open.
Montgomerie, too, has Royal Troon on his mind, saying his main goal now is to win the third major at the course where his father James is the secretary.
Australia's Robert Allenby, who beat German Bernhard Langer in a play-off last year, defends in Paris. ($ = 0.599 British Pounds)
